title: The monsters that hang on springs
target: Why a family of monsters in R.E.P.O. wobbles: their heads, ears, tails and eyes hang on springs with targets of their own, and the game keeps a whole second set of sounds for when they change size.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A level with one of the spring-built monsters in it
A crew spread out enough to hear which sound came from where
Room to back off rather than stand your ground

steps.do: Expect some monsters to be built as parts that hang on springs rather than as one rigid body.
steps.because: the elsa's head, tails and ears each have a spring with a transform and a target of their own (headSpring, headTransform, tail01Spring, tail01TransformTarget, ear01Spring, ear01TransformL)

steps.do: Read a swinging part as the spring doing its work rather than as an animation.
steps.because: its jaw, feet and idle and wiggle transforms are sprung separately from the head (jawSpring, jawTransform, feetTransform, headIdleTransform, headWiggleTransform)

steps.do: Expect the whole set of springs to move together, because they share two multipliers.
steps.because: the hanging parts share a speed multiplier and a damping multiplier (springSpeedMultiplier, springDampingMultiplier)

steps.do: Do not judge a monster's size from the model alone, because it carries two colliders.
steps.because: it keeps a collider for its small size and one for its big size, placed apart from the visuals (smallColliderTransform, bigColliderTransform)

steps.do: Expect the game to keep different art for the two sizes.
steps.because: it ships one fur texture for the small size and a different one for the big size (Elsa Fur Small, Elsa Fur Big)

steps.do: Listen for the change between sizes, because it is staged with its own sounds.
steps.because: the change has a start, a stinger, limbs breaking, the head looking up and a landing, each with a sound of its own (transformStartSound, transformStingerSound, transformLimbBreakSound, transformHeadLookUpSound, transformLandSound)

steps.do: Expect each of its noises to exist twice, small and big.
steps.because: barks, footsteps, hurt, jump, landing, death and panting are each kept in a small version and a big version (barkSmallSound, barkBigSoundLocal, footstepSmallSound, hurtSmallSound, landBigSound, deathBigSound)

steps.do: Know that a big bark is not always just for you.
steps.because: one of its big barks has a version for nearby players and a version for everyone (barkBigSoundLocal, barkBigSoundGlobal)

steps.do: Expect another monster to be built the same way, with its own change of form.
steps.because: the duck monster's body and head each hang on a spring with a target of their own, and it has a sound for a change of form (bodySpring, bodyTransform, headLookAtSpring, transformSound)

steps.do: Watch a bowtie monster's whole body turn rather than only its head.
steps.because: its head and both eyes are sprung with targets of their own, and the body turns on a horizontal and a vertical spring (headSpring, eyeRightSpring, horizontalRotationSpring, verticalRotationSpring)

commonMistakes: Reading a spring-built monster as stiff and standing next to it.
Judging which size you are facing from the artwork rather than from how it behaves.
Treating a change of size as silent when the change has a whole set of sounds.
Assuming a big bark is only for the players close enough to see it.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
